items.followUp: What is the effect of nondisjunction during meiosis? Give one example of a resulting disorder.

rubric.why: Identifies the error and its direct effect on chromosome number.
rubric.description: Nondisjunction is the failure of chromosomes or chromatids to separate properly during cell division, producing cells or gametes with an abnormal chromosome number.
rubric.how: Award for describing failed separation and the resulting abnormal chromosome number.

rubric.why: Gives a valid example of a condition caused by nondisjunction.
rubric.description: An abnormal chromosome number may cause a genetic disorder such as Down syndrome.
rubric.how: Award for naming a valid example, such as Down syndrome.

modelAnswer: Nondisjunction is the failure of chromosomes or chromatids to separate properly during cell division.
It produces cells or gametes with an abnormal chromosome number, which can cause disorders such as Down syndrome.

items.followUp: What is a reaction centre in a photosystem?

rubric.why: Identifies the pigment-containing unit and its location.
rubric.description: A photosystem is a group of light-absorbing pigments and proteins in the thylakoid membrane.
rubric.how: Award for identifying the pigment group and its location in the thylakoid membrane.

rubric.why: Shows the role of the photosystem in photosynthesis.
rubric.description: The photosystem captures light energy and transfers it to its reaction centre during photosynthesis.
rubric.how: Award for stating that it captures or transfers light energy for photosynthesis.

modelAnswer: A photosystem is a group of light-absorbing pigments and proteins present in the thylakoid membrane of a chloroplast.
It captures light energy and transfers it to a reaction centre during photosynthesis.

items.followUp: Write the balanced equation for cellular respiration.

rubric.why: Checks the correct reactants and glucose product in the balanced equation.
rubric.description: The equation includes six molecules each of carbon dioxide and water and one molecule of glucose.
rubric.how: Award for the correct reactants and glucose product with their coefficients.

rubric.why: Checks the oxygen product and the conditions shown for photosynthesis.
rubric.description: The equation includes six molecules of oxygen and indicates light and chlorophyll above the arrow.
rubric.how: Award for oxygen with its coefficient and the light/chlorophyll conditions.

rubric.why: Identifies the linked, enzyme-controlled nature of a metabolic pathway.
rubric.description: A metabolic pathway is a series of enzyme-controlled chemical reactions in a cell.
rubric.how: Award for describing a series of reactions controlled by enzymes.

rubric.why: Shows that reactions proceed through changes from starting substances to products.
rubric.description: In a pathway, the product of one reaction may become the substrate for the next, forming intermediates on the way to the final product.
rubric.how: Award for explaining the sequential conversion through intermediates to a final product.

modelAnswer: A metabolic pathway is a series of enzyme-controlled chemical reactions that occur in a cell.
The product of one reaction may become the substrate for the next, forming intermediates before the final product.

items.followUp: How can a change in pH affect the activity of an enzyme?

rubric.why: Explains what denaturation does to the enzyme’s structure.
rubric.description: Enzyme denaturation is a change in an enzyme’s three-dimensional shape, including its active site.
rubric.how: Award for stating that denaturation changes the enzyme’s shape or active site.

rubric.why: Explains the consequence of denaturation for enzyme action.
rubric.description: The substrate no longer fits the altered active site, so enzyme activity is reduced or stops.
rubric.how: Award for explaining that substrate binding or enzyme action is impaired.

modelAnswer: Enzyme denaturation is a change in an enzyme’s three-dimensional shape, including the shape of its active site.
The substrate no longer fits the active site, so enzyme action is reduced or stops.

items.followUp: What is a sink in the translocation of food in plants? Give one example.

rubric.why: Defines a source in plant food transport.
rubric.description: A source is a plant part where food is produced or released for transport.
rubric.how: Award for identifying a source as the site where food is produced or released.

rubric.why: Provides a suitable example of a plant source.
rubric.description: Leaves are an example of a source because they produce food by photosynthesis.
rubric.how: Award for giving leaves or another suitable food-producing plant part as an example.

modelAnswer: A source is a plant part where food is produced or released for transport.
Leaves are an example of a source because they produce food by photosynthesis.

items.followUp: Give two ways in which biology is useful in medicine and two ways it is useful in farming.

rubric.why: Explains the contribution of biology to medical work.
rubric.description: Biology helps people understand, diagnose and treat diseases and develop medicines or vaccines.
rubric.how: Award one mark for relevant medical applications, such as understanding or diagnosing disease, and one for treatment or developing medicines/vaccines.

rubric.why: Explains the contribution of biology to farming and food supply.
rubric.description: Biology helps improve crops and farm production, including controlling pests and diseases.
rubric.how: Award one mark for improving crops or yield and one for another valid farming application, such as pest or disease control.

modelAnswer: Biology is important in medicine because it helps us understand, diagnose and treat diseases.
Biological knowledge is used to develop medicines and vaccines.
Biology is important in farming because it helps improve crops and increase food production.
It also helps farmers control crop pests and diseases.

items.followUp: Name the three types of muscle tissue and give one characteristic of each.

rubric.why: Defines muscle tissue by its contractile nature.
rubric.description: Muscle tissue consists of contractile cells or fibres that produce movement by contraction.
rubric.how: Award for defining muscle tissue as contractile cells or fibres.

rubric.why: Identifies skeletal muscle and a distinguishing feature.
rubric.description: Skeletal muscle is striated, voluntary and usually attached to bones.
rubric.how: Award for naming skeletal muscle and giving a correct feature or location.

rubric.why: Identifies smooth muscle and a distinguishing feature.
rubric.description: Smooth muscle is non-striated and involuntary, and occurs in the walls of internal organs.
rubric.how: Award for naming smooth muscle and giving a correct feature or location.

rubric.why: Identifies cardiac muscle and its characteristic features and location.
rubric.description: Cardiac muscle is striated, involuntary muscle found in the heart; its cells are branched.
rubric.how: Award one mark for identifying cardiac muscle and its heart location, and one for a correct feature such as branched, striated or involuntary.

modelAnswer: Muscle tissue consists of contractile cells or fibres that produce movement by contraction.
Skeletal muscle is striated and voluntary; it is usually attached to bones.
Smooth muscle is non-striated and involuntary; it is found in the walls of internal organs.
Cardiac muscle is striated and involuntary; its branched cells form the muscle of the heart.
